prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
competitors_mentioned: Texas Dept. of Licensing and Regulation
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right one depends on your location in Houston, whether it’s a residential or commercial job, whether it’s an emergency, your budget, and the make/model of your system. I can, however, help you pick a great contractor and give a short list of well-regarded options if you want.

Quick checklist to find the best Houston AC repair company for you
- Verify license and insurance: Confirm the contractor is licensed in Texas (check Texas Dept. of Licensing and Regulation) and carries liability insurance.
- Look for NATE-certified technicians and experience with your system’s brand.
- Check recent reviews: Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and BBB for complaints/resolution.
- Ask about response time and 24/7 emergency service if you need it now.
- Get a written estimate (diagnostic fee, repair parts/labor, warranty on parts and labor).
- Compare at least 2–3 quotes — beware of very low-ball offers.
- Ask about flat-rate vs. hourly pricing, permits (if needed), and disposal of old equipment.
- Red flags: no license, only cash payments, high-pressure sales to replace units without diagnostics, no written warranty.

Companies commonly recommended in Houston
- John Moore Services (Houston-based, long-standing presence)
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (franchise with local offices)
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (national chain that serves Houston)
- One Hour Heating & Air (local franchise)
Note: availability, pricing, and quality vary by neighborhood and franchise. Independently owned local contractors often provide excellent service too — vet them with the checklist above.

If you want, I can:
- Find the top-rated HVAC repair companies in your ZIP code and compare reviews/warranties (tell me your ZIP and whether it’s residential or commercial), or
- Provide a short phone/email script and a list of questions to ask when getting quotes.

Which would you prefer?
